formulas.name: Kadane's Algorithm — Max Sum Subarray
formulas.formula:
curr = max(A[i], curr + A[i]) // best sum ENDING at i
best = max(best, curr) // best seen anywhere
// init: curr = best = A[0]
formulas.example: Ex: A=[-2,1,-3,4,-1,2,1,-5,4] → best = 6 (subarray [4,-1,2,1])
whenToUse: Maximum sum of a contiguous subarray
Any "running accumulation that may restart from scratch"
All-negative input → answer is the largest element, not 0
formulas.note: Never seed best = 0 — that silently returns 0 for all-negative arrays. Initialise both curr and best to A[0] (or Integer.MIN_VALUE).

formulas.name: 2D Contribution — Sum of All Submatrices
formulas.formula:
answer = Σi Σj A[i][j] * (i+1)(N−i) * (j+1)(M−j)
// (i+1)(N−i) = # row-ranges covering row i
// (j+1)(M−j) = # col-ranges covering col j
formulas.example: Ex: 2×2 grid of 1s → each cell counted (i+1)(N−i)(j+1)(M−j)=4 times → total 16
whenToUse: "Sum of f over all submatrices" of a grid
2D extension of the subarray contribution trick
Replaces O(N²M²) enumeration with O(N·M)
formulas.note: The 1D analogue is contribution(A[i]) = A[i]·(i+1)·(N−i); the 2D form just multiplies the independent row-count and column-count of ranges.

formulas.name: Why 32 Bits? (int width)
formulas.formula:
// Java int is FIXED at 32 bits → bits 0..31
for (int i = 0; i < 32; i++) { ... } // covers every bit
// bit 31 = sign bit (two's complement)
// walk with >>> (unsigned), NOT >>, so the sign bit doesn't smear
formulas.example: Count set bits: int c=0; for(int i=0;i<32;i++) if((n>>>i & 1)==1) c++; — 32 iterations cover all of int, including negatives.
whenToUse: Looping over bits, building masks, reverse-bits, count-set-bits
Input is a "32-bit signed integer" (the usual LeetCode constraint = int range)
Use long + loop to 64 instead when values exceed int
formulas.note: Java guarantees int=32 bits, long=64 (unlike C, where int width is platform-dependent). Bit 31 is the sign, so for negatives use unsigned shift >>> — plain >> copies the sign bit and loops forever / misreads high bits.

formulas.name: Min-XOR Pair = Adjacent After Sort
formulas.formula:
sort(A);
min XOR over all pairs == min over ADJACENT pairs
answer = mini ( A[i] ^ A[i+1] ) // only N−1 pairs
// small XOR ⇔ longer shared leading-bit prefix
formulas.example: Ex: A=[0,2,5,7] → check 0^2=2, 2^5=7, 5^7=2 → min 2. No skipped pair beats it (0^5=5, 2^7=5, 0^7=7).
whenToUse: "Minimum XOR of any two elements" in an array
Turning a brute O(N²) all-pairs scan into O(N log N) sort + linear sweep
Any "closest two values" argument that rides on shared high bits
formulas.note: Why adjacent suffices: for sorted a ≤ b ≤ c, the middle b shares at least as many leading bits with each neighbor as the neighbors share with each other, so a^c can never be strictly smaller than both a^b and b^c — the minimum can't "jump over" b. Hence only neighbouring pairs can win.

formulas.name: Bitwise Independence (per-bit decomposition)
formulas.formula:
// AND / OR / XOR act on each bit position alone — NO carry between bits
answer = Σb=0..31 ( solveForBit(b) ) << b
// a 32-bit problem splits into 32 independent 1-bit problems
formulas.example: Ex: Σ A[i] = Σb (count of numbers with bit b set) × 2b — each bit tallied on its own, then weighted.
whenToUse: Build an answer bit-by-bit (decide each output bit separately)
Single Number II/III: count set bits per position, take mod k
Anything where you can ask "what happens at bit b?" in isolation
formulas.note: Unlike + − × (which carry across bits), bitwise ops don't — so you may treat each of the 32 columns as a separate, tiny problem and recombine with << b. This is the foundation for bit contribution counting.

formulas.name: Bit Contribution Counting
formulas.formula:
// per bit b: k = #numbers with bit b SET, n = total
Σ XOR over all pairs = Σb k(n−k) · 2b
Σ AND over all pairs = Σb C(k,2) · 2b
Σ OR  over all pairs = Σb ( C(n,2) − C(n−k,2) ) · 2b
formulas.example: Ex (XOR pairs): A=[1,2,3], bit0 set in {1,3} → k=2, n−k=1 → 2·1=2 pairs contribute 20; bit1 set in {2,3} → k=2 → 2 pairs contribute 21. Total = 2·1 + 2·2 = 6.
whenToUse: "Sum of XOR / AND / OR over all pairs (or subarrays)"
Replace O(N²) all-pairs enumeration with O(32·N)
Count, per bit, how often it survives into the result
formulas.note: Rides on bitwise independence: a bit shows in the result of k·(n−k) XOR-pairs (one set, one unset), C(k,2) AND-pairs (both set), or C(n,2)−C(n−k,2) OR-pairs (at least one set). Multiply each count by 2b and sum.

formulas.name: GCD (Euclidean algorithm)
formulas.formula:
gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b) // until b == 0
gcd(a, 0) = a
formulas.example: Ex: gcd(48, 18) → gcd(18, 12) → gcd(12, 6) → gcd(6, 0) = 6
whenToUse: Reducing fractions / simplifying ratios
"Largest equal-size group" problems
LCM derivation (needs gcd)
Stride / cycle problems on arrays
formulas.note: Recursive form is O(log(min(a, b))). Iterative while (b != 0) { t = b; b = a % b; a = t; } avoids stack frames.

formulas.name: LCM (via GCD)
formulas.formula: lcm(a, b) = (a / gcd(a, b)) * b
formulas.example: Ex: lcm(4, 6) = (4 / gcd(4,6)) * 6 = (4 / 2) * 6 = 12
whenToUse: Aligning two cyclic events
"Smallest number divisible by both"
Period of repeating patterns
formulas.note: Always divide first, then multiply — a * b / gcd can overflow even when the result fits.

formulas.name: Sum of First N Natural Numbers
formulas.formula: 1 + 2 + … + N = N * (N + 1) / 2
formulas.example: Ex: N = 10 → 10 * 11 / 2 = 55
whenToUse: "Find the missing number in 1..N"
Counting total subarrays of an array (N*(N+1)/2)
Triangular number / staircase totals
Brute upper bound for staircase / sqrt problems
formulas.note: Always use long — N=10⁵ already gives ~5·10⁹, overflows int.

formulas.name: Sum of Squares 1..N
formulas.formula: 1² + 2² + … + N² = N * (N + 1) * (2N + 1) / 6
formulas.example: Ex: N=4 → 4·5·9/6 = 30 (1+4+9+16)
whenToUse: Closed-form for nested sums
Estimating brute-force work over partial sums

formulas.name: Total Subarrays of an Array
formulas.formula: #subarrays(N) = N * (N + 1) / 2
formulas.example: Ex: N=4 → 4·5/2 = 10 subarrays
whenToUse: Sanity-checking that "sum of contributions" equals total work
Choosing whether O(N²) enumeration even fits
formulas.note: Identical to "sum of 1..N" — every left endpoint l pairs with N - l right endpoints.

formulas.name: Inclusion–Exclusion (divisible by A or B)
formulas.formula:
#(1..N divisible by A or B)
  = ⌊N / A⌋ + ⌊N / B⌋ − ⌊N / lcm(A, B)⌋
formulas.example: Ex: N=12, A=2, B=3 → 6 + 4 − 2 = 8 (numbers: 2,3,4,6,8,9,10,12).
whenToUse: "K-th magical number divisible by A or B"
BS on answer where the predicate is "count ≤ mid ≥ K"
Any two-set "OR" count over [1..N]
formulas.note: Subtraction prevents double-counting multiples of lcm(A,B). Generalizes to 3+ sets with alternating signs.

formulas.name: Safe Modulo of Subtraction (avoid negatives)
formulas.formula: result = ((a − b) % MOD + MOD) % MOD
formulas.example: Ex: a=3, b=10, MOD=7 → (-7 % 7 + 7) % 7 = 0. Without the +MOD, Java would return −0 or a negative depending on language.
whenToUse: Any modular running sum that involves subtraction
"Max − min" contribution sums with mod
formulas.note: In Java, % on negatives returns negative — always wrap with + MOD) % MOD after any subtraction.

formulas.name: Modular Product (long cast)
formulas.formula: (a * b) % MOD = ((long)a * b) % MOD
formulas.example: Ex: a=b=10⁵, int * int overflows; (long)a * b = 10¹⁰ fits in long.
whenToUse: Any product where both operands can reach √MAX_LONG
Contribution sums multiplying counts × values

formulas.name: Safe Mid (no overflow)
formulas.formula: mid = low + (high - low) / 2
formulas.example: Ex: low=2·10⁹, high=2·10⁹+8 → naive (low+high)/2 overflows int; safe form stays valid.
whenToUse: Every binary search — no exception
Especially: BS on answer space where bounds can be 10⁹
formulas.note: Mathematically equivalent to (low+high)/2 — but immune to int overflow when low, high are near MAX_INT.

formulas.name: Matrix Median Position
formulas.formula: target rank = (N * M + 1) / 2 // 1-indexed median in odd-size matrix
formulas.example: Ex: 3×5 matrix → (15+1)/2 = 8th smallest is the median.
whenToUse: Median of a row-wise sorted matrix
BS on value range + per-row lower_bound

formulas.name: Lower Bound (count ≤ x in sorted row)
formulas.formula:
count(≤ x) = upper_bound(row, x) − 0
count(< x) = lower_bound(row, x)
formulas.example: Ex: row = [3,8,14,22], x=10 → upper=2 (3,8 ≤ 10), lower=2 (same since 10 missing).
whenToUse: Count "how many ≤ candidate" across N sorted rows in O(N log M)
BS-on-value-range driver function

formulas.name: Integer Square Root via BS
formulas.formula:
⌊√N⌋ = largest mid with mid * mid ≤ N
// search space: low=0, high=N (or 46341 cap if N fits in int)
// use (long) cast on mid*mid to avoid overflow
formulas.example: Ex: N=11 → mid=3 (9 ≤ 11 ✓), mid=4 (16 > 11 ✗) → 3.
whenToUse: "⌊√N⌋ without Math.sqrt"
Staircase: smallest k with k(k+1)/2 ≥ N
Any "largest x with monotone predicate"
formulas.note: Cast: long sq = (long) mid * mid; — int*int overflows when N ≥ 2³¹.

formulas.name: BS-on-Answer Bounds
formulas.formula:
// minimize-max (painters, books, paint cost):
low = max(items) // can't go below largest single item
high = sum(items) // 1 worker takes everything

// maximize-min (aggressive cows):
low = 1 // smallest gap
high = max(items) − min(items) // widest possible gap
formulas.example: Painters [10, 20, 30, 40]: low=40, high=100. Feasible(70)? → yes → try 60.
whenToUse: BS on answer space — picking the right bounds is half the work
Wrong bounds (low=0 or low=1 for minimize-max) → infinite-loop or wrong answer

formulas.name: Pivot Detection in Rotated Sorted Array
formulas.formula:
// At each step exactly one half is sorted:
if (A[low] ≤ A[mid]) → left half is sorted
else → right half is sorted

// Then check if target lies inside the sorted half:
if (target in [A[low], A[mid])) → go left, else → go right
formulas.example: Ex: A=[4,5,6,7,0,1,2], target=0. mid=3 (A[mid]=7). A[low]=4 ≤ 7 → left sorted, target 0 ∉ [4,7), go right.
whenToUse: Search in a rotated sorted array (no duplicates)
Find min in rotated sorted array (same half-test)
formulas.note: Use <= not < on the left-sorted check — handles the case where low == mid.

formulas.name: Median by Partition (Two Sorted Arrays)
formulas.formula:
// Let N ≤ M; BS over partitionA in [0..N]:
partitionA = (low + high) / 2
partitionB = (N + M + 1) / 2 − partitionA

// Valid when:
maxLeftA ≤ minRightB && maxLeftB ≤ minRightA

// Median:
odd → max(maxLeftA, maxLeftB)
even → (max(maxLeftA, maxLeftB) + min(minRightA, minRightB)) / 2.0
formulas.example: Ex: A=[1,3], B=[2]. N=1, M=2. Trying partitionA=1, partitionB=1 → maxLeftA=1, minRightB=∞, maxLeftB=2, minRightA=3 → valid → median = max(1,2) = 2.
whenToUse: Median of two sorted arrays in O(log(min(N, M)))
K-th element of two sorted arrays (similar partition trick)
formulas.note: Use Integer.MIN_VALUE / MAX_VALUE as sentinels when a partition lands at the array edge.

formulas.name: Min-Stack Encode/Decode (O(1) extra space)
formulas.formula:
// push x:
if (stack empty) → push x, min = x
else if (x >= min) → push x
else → push (2*x − min), min = x

// top:
if (top < min) → return min // encoded marker
else → return top

// pop:
if (top < min) → min = 2*min − top // recover old min
then pop
formulas.example: Why it works: when new x < min, store the "deviation" 2x−min. Since 2x−min < x < min, it acts as a sentinel; on pop we reverse to get the previous min.
whenToUse: Min/Max stack with O(1) per op and O(1) extra space
Interview classic when "no auxiliary stack" is required
formulas.note: Use long if values can be near MAX_INT — 2*x − min can underflow int.

formulas.name: Contribution Technique — Subarray Sum
formulas.formula:
contribution(A[i]) = A[i] * (i − L) * (R − i)
// L = prev boundary index, R = next boundary index
// (i − L) = # subarrays where i is the chosen left side
// (R − i) = # subarrays where i is the chosen right side
formulas.example: Why it works: every subarray (l, r) containing i has exactly one "i" — sum across all subarrays = Σ A[i] × (ways i is included).
whenToUse: "Sum of f(subarray) over all subarrays"
f is min, max, sum, or count of a single element
Naive O(N²) or O(N³) is too slow
formulas.note: L and R come from prevSmaller / nextSmaller (for min contribution) or prevGreater / nextGreater (for max contribution) — built once with a monotonic stack in O(N).

formulas.name: Contribution to Min & Max Stack Sum
formulas.formula:
answer = Σ A[i] * (i − PG[i]) * (NG[i] − i)
       − Σ A[i] * (i − PS[i]) * (NS[i] − i)
// PG/NG = prev/next Greater · PS/NS = prev/next Smaller
formulas.example: Reads as: "every element contributes A[i] × (# subarrays where it's the max) MINUS A[i] × (# where it's the min)".
whenToUse: Σ (max(sub) − min(sub)) over all subarrays
Distinct-element handling: use > on one side, >= on the other to avoid double-count
formulas.note: Tie-breaking matters: for "next greater" use strict >, for "prev greater" use >= (or vice versa) so each subarray is counted exactly once.

formulas.name: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
formulas.formula:
area(i) = H[i] * (NS[i] − PS[i] − 1)
answer = max over all i of area(i)
formulas.example: Ex: H=[2,1,5,6,2,3] → at i=3 (H=6): PS=2, NS=4, area = 6 * (4−2−1) = 6; at i=2 (H=5): PS=1, NS=4, area = 5*2 = 10 ← max.
whenToUse: Maximum rectangle inside a bar chart
Building block for "max rectangle in binary matrix"

formulas.name: Sliding-Window Min / Max via Deque
formulas.formula:
// Window is valid for i ≥ B − 1
answer[i] = A[deque.peekFirst()]
// Maintain decreasing deque for MAX, increasing for MIN
evict from front: while front index < i − B + 1
evict from back: while A[back] ≤ A[i] (for max)
whenToUse: Fixed-size window max/min in O(N) (not O(N·B))
Σ window-max + window-min over all windows
formulas.note: Each index enters and leaves the deque at most once → amortized O(1) per step → O(N) total.

formulas.name: Balanced-Tree Check
formulas.formula:
isBalanced(node):
  hL = height(left), hR = height(right)
  return |hL − hR| ≤ 1 && isBalanced(left) && isBalanced(right)

// O(N) trick: return -1 from height() if any subtree is unbalanced
heightOrFail(node):
  if (hL == -1 || hR == -1 || |hL−hR| > 1) return −1
formulas.example: Ex: tree with hL=2, hR=4 at root → |2−4| = 2 → NOT balanced.
whenToUse: AVL property check (every node)
Any "no two subtrees differ by more than k"
formulas.note: The "-1 sentinel" trick avoids re-computing height per recursion call — turns O(N²) into O(N).

formulas.name: BST Validity (range carry)
formulas.formula:
isBST(node, min, max):
  if (node == null) return true
  if (node.val ≤ min || node.val ≥ max) return false
  return isBST(left, min, node.val) && isBST(right, node.val, max)

// initial call: isBST(root, Long.MIN_VALUE, Long.MAX_VALUE)
formulas.example: Why long: a node with val = Integer.MIN_VALUE would fail the int-range check at the root — promote bounds to long.
whenToUse: Validate BST property recursively
Any "every node must respect ancestor constraints"

formulas.name: Height of a Node
formulas.formula:
height(null) = −1 // or 0, depending on convention
height(node) = 1 + max(height(left), height(right))
formulas.example: Ex: single root → height = 0 (or 1). Leaf with two null kids → 1 + max(−1,−1) = 0.
whenToUse: Max depth / min depth
Diameter of a tree (longest path through a node)
Balanced-tree check (|hL − hR| ≤ 1 at every node)

formulas.name: Subtree Sum / Path Sum Recurrence
formulas.formula:
subtreeSum(node) = node.val + subtreeSum(left) + subtreeSum(right)
pathSum(node, target) = pathSum(left, target − node.val) || pathSum(right, …)
formulas.example: Sum-tree check: node.val == subtreeSum(left) + subtreeSum(right) at every internal node.
whenToUse: "Does any root-to-leaf path sum to B?"
Sum tree validation
Equal tree partition (split sum / 2)

formulas.name: BST Range Pruning
formulas.example: Why it's fast: we skip entire subtrees that can't contain a valid value — average O(log N + K) for K hits.
whenToUse: "Count / list nodes in [L, R] inside a BST"
BST search, delete, validate — all use the same pruning idea

formulas.name: Level-Order Index Map (heap-style)
formulas.formula:
// For a complete tree stored in array at index i (1-indexed):
left(i) = 2 * i
right(i) = 2 * i + 1
parent(i) = i / 2
formulas.example: 0-indexed: left = 2i+1, right = 2i+2, parent = (i−1)/2.
whenToUse: Serialize / deserialize complete binary trees
Heap implementation (priority queue)
Segment tree layout
